headline: Baidu Ships a Vast Base Model
lede: ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base arrives as a 280-billion-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts model with a one-million-token inference window. The FP8 and BF16 weights give researchers a starting point for fine-tuning, reasoning, and agent experiments.

headline: A Residential Proxy Reaches the White House
lede: An IP associated with the White House network appeared inside a commercial residential-proxy service. The finding is a warning about accountability and opaque bandwidth markets, not proof that the building itself was compromised.

headline: Lemmings Turn the Page Into a Playground
lede: Tiny walkers now tumble across borders, buttons, images, and lines of text in a browser-based CSS animation. Resize the window, rearrange the page, and watch ordinary layout become a small physics engine.

headline: The Awesome List Has a Maintenance Problem
lede: GitHub’s curated lists once offered a dependable path through unfamiliar tools and projects. As links decay and AI-generated noise multiplies, their usefulness depends less on the format than on the humans willing to keep editing it.
pullquote: A list is only as trustworthy as the maintenance behind it.

headline: AI Finds Hundreds of Kernel Exploits
lede: OpenAI reports an automated pipeline that reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and generated 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits. The result makes patching, validation, and maintainer coordination harder to postpone.

headline: OpenAI Adds GIFs to Its Image Engine
lede: Images 2.6 brings faster generation, targeted markup edits, SVG export, and animated output to ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. Its new Flare and Sunburst variants trade speed against fidelity while developers continue to test how much control the system really affords.

headline: CSS Replaces Video in Tiny Product Demos
lede: A set of ten-second feature clips uses HTML, CSS keyframes, tokens, and responsive layout instead of video or JavaScript. The demos stay sharp, editable, and accessible, though they remain illustrations rather than substitutes for a real workflow.

headline: Zig Makes Ambiguous Operators Stop
lede: Zig’s partial operator precedence keeps familiar expressions while demanding parentheses where combinations become unclear. The same devlog adds package diagnostics, pointer-stability checks, and sturdier SPIR-V and LLVM backends.

headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro Opens a Trillion-Parameter Frontier
lede: Moonshot AI has released weights for a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with a one-million-token context window and demanding deployment requirements. The release is accessible in principle, but its hardware, licensing, and tool-call constraints put the experiment beyond most personal machines.

headline: Ripple Makes a Smaller Case for Coding Models
lede: Ripple-65B Preview pairs a dense architecture with twelve trillion training tokens and a reported 80.52 TerminalBench score. Its open weights and efficiency story are intriguing, while the narrow comparisons leave the claimed lead open to inspection.
